title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Model Format for First Instance Administrative Judgment (Trial Implementation)
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the "Form for First Instance Administrative Judgment (Trial Implementation)"

Fa Fa [2004] No. 25

To the High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

To standardize the form of administrative judgment documents and improve the quality of their preparation, the Supreme People's Court's "Form for First Instance Administrative Judgment (Trial Implementation)" is hereby issued to you for trial application in judicial practice. Any issues encountered during the trial should be promptly reported to our Court.

December 8, 2004

Form for First Instance Administrative Judgment (Trial Implementation)

Form One

___ People's Court

Administrative Judgment

(For first instance administrative action cases)

(___ ) ___ Xing Chu Zi No. ___

Plaintiff ... (state the name or title and other basic information).

Legal representative ... (state the name, gender, and position).

Agent ad litem (or appointed agent, statutory agent) ... (state the name and other basic information).

Defendant ... (state the name of the administrative entity and its address).

Legal representative ... (state the name, gender, and position).

Agent ad litem ... (state the name and other basic information).

Third party ... (state the name or title and other basic information).

Legal representative ... (state the name, gender, and position).

Agent ad litem (or appointed agent, statutory agent) ... (state the name and other basic information).

The plaintiff ___, dissatisfied with (name of administrative entity) (specific administrative act), filed an administrative lawsuit with this Court on ___ year ___ month ___ day. After accepting the case on ___ year ___ month ___ day, this Court served a copy of the complaint and the notification of response to the defendant on ___ year ___ month ___ day. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and held a public (or closed) hearing on ___ year ___ month ___ day. ... (state the parties, agents ad litem, witnesses, appraisers, inspectors, interpreters, etc. who participated in the hearing) attended the proceedings. ... (state other important procedural activities that occurred, such as the approval of an extension of the trial period, etc.). The trial of this case has now concluded.

The defendant (name of administrative entity) (state the administrative procedure for making the specific administrative act) made a ___ number _____ decision (or other name) against the plaintiff on ___ year ___ month ___ day, ... (detail the facts found by the specific administrative act under suit, the legal norms applied, and the content of the decision). The defendant provided to this Court on ___ year ___ month ___ day the evidence and basis for making the specific administrative act under suit (if there was a court-approved extension for providing evidence, it should be stated): 1.... (name and content of evidence), proving ... (state the purpose of the evidence. The purpose may be summarized and categorized according to the defendant's sequence of evidence presentation; or, depending on the case, evidence and basis may be classified and listed from aspects such as statutory authority, enforcement procedure, fact-finding, and application of law; or evidence may be comprehensively listed with non-contentious parts briefly stated).

The plaintiff ___ alleges: ... (summarize the plaintiff's claims and reasons, and the evidence provided by the plaintiff).

The defendant ___ defends: ... (summarize the main grounds and requests of the defendant's defense).

The third party ___ states: ... (summarize the main opinions of the third party, and evidence provided by the third party).

This Court, in accordance with the law (or upon application by the plaintiff or third party), obtained the following evidence: ....

Following in-court examination of evidence (or exchange of evidence), this Court makes the following determination regarding the evidence: ....

Upon trial, it is found that: ... (the facts of the case as established upon trial).

This Court holds: ... (analyze and demonstrate the legality of the specific administrative act using substantive and procedural legal norms of administrative law, analyze each party's grounds for litigation in turn, evaluate whether they are established, state whether they are supported or adopted, and provide reasons). In accordance with the provisions of ... (state the articles, paragraphs, items, and sub-items of the Administrative Procedure Law and relevant judicial interpretations on which the judgment is based), the judgment is as follows:

... (state the judgment result), divided into the following nine situations:

First, when maintaining the specific administrative act under suit, state:

Maintain the (name of administrative entity) ___ year ___ month ___ day (___ ) ___ Zi No. ___ ... (name of specific administrative act).

Second, when revoking the specific administrative act under suit, state:

1. Revoke the (name of administrative entity) ___ year ___ month ___ day (___ ) ___ Zi No. ___ ... (name of specific administrative act);

2. Order (name of administrative entity) to make a new specific administrative act within ___ days (if re-making is not required, this item is not written; if a time limit is not appropriate, the time limit is not written).

Third, when partially revoking the specific administrative act under suit, state:

1. Maintain item ___ of the (name of administrative entity) ___ year ___ month ___ day (___ ) ___ Zi No. ___ ... (name of specific administrative act), i.e., ... (state the specific content maintained);

2. Revoke item ___ of the (name of administrative entity) ___ year ___ month ___ day (___ ) ___ Zi No. ___ ... (name of specific administrative act), i.e., ... (state the specific content revoked);

3. Order (name of administrative entity) to make a new specific administrative act within ___ days (if re-making is not required, this item is not written; if a time limit is not appropriate, the time limit is not written).

Fourth, when ordering a change to an administrative penalty, state:

Change the (name of administrative entity) ___ year ___ month ___ day (___ ) ___ Zi No. ___ administrative penalty decision (or administrative reconsideration decision, or other specific administrative act of an administrative penalty nature) to ... (state the changed content).

Fifth, when dismissing the plaintiff's claims, state:

Dismiss the plaintiff's claim for revocation (or change, or confirmation of illegality, etc.) of the (name of administrative entity) ___ year ___ month ___ day (___ ) ___ Zi No. ___ ... (name of specific administrative act).

Sixth, when confirming that the specific administrative act under suit is lawful or valid, state:

Confirm that the (name of administrative entity) ___ year ___ month ___ day (___ ) ___ Zi No. ___ ... (name of specific administrative act) is lawful (or valid).

Seventh, when confirming that the specific administrative act under suit is unlawful (or invalid), state:

1. Confirm that the (name of administrative entity) ___ year ___ month ___ day (___ ) ___ Zi No. ___ ... (name of specific administrative act) is unlawful (or invalid).

2. Order that within ... (specified time limit), ... (state the remedial measures to be taken. If no remedial measures are needed, this item is not written).

Eighth, when dismissing the plaintiff's claim for compensation, state:

Dismiss the plaintiff ___'s claim for compensation regarding ... (compensation claim matters).

Ninth, when ordering the defendant to pay compensation, state:

(Name of administrative entity) shall, within ___ days from the effective date of this judgment, compensate the plaintiff ___ ... (state the amount of compensation).

... (state the allocation of litigation costs).

If dissatisfied with this judgment, an appeal may be filed within fifteen days from the date of service of the judgment. The appellant shall submit a notice of appeal to this Court and provide copies of the notice of appeal in accordance with the number of opposing parties, appealing to the ___ People's Court.

Presiding Judge ___

Judge ___

Judge ___

___ year ___ month ___ day

(Court seal)

This document is verified to be identical to the original.

Court Clerk ___

Appendix: (If necessary, relevant content from the judgment may be included in an appendix)

Explanatory Notes for Form One

I. Heading

The heading shall sequentially include the title, case number, basic information of the parties and their agents ad litem, as well as the origin of the case, the composition of the trial panel, and the hearing process.

1. The name of the court in the title shall generally be consistent with the text on the court seal, but basic-level courts shall include the name of the province, municipality, or autonomous region.

2. The case number is a sequential identifier for different cases and shall follow the principle of one case per number. The case number consists of the year of case filing, the court that made the judgment, the nature of the case, the abbreviation for the trial procedure, and the case sequence number. For example, the first instance administrative case No. 1 of 2002 at the Huangpu District People's Court of Shanghai is expressed as "(2002) Huang Xing Chu Zi No. 1".

3. Plaintiffs who initiate administrative lawsuits include citizens, legal persons, or other organizations.

Where the plaintiff is a citizen, state the name, gender, date of birth, ethnicity, place of origin, and address. For a citizen, the address shall be the domicile; if the domicile and the habitual residence differ, state the habitual residence. Where the plaintiff is a legal person, state the name and address of the legal person, and separately list on a new line the legal representative's name, gender, and position. Where the plaintiff is another organization without legal person status, state its name or business name and address, and separately list on a new line the litigation representative's name, gender, and position. Where the plaintiff is an individual industrial or commercial household, state the owner's name, gender, date of birth, ethnicity, place of origin, and address; if a business name is used, state in parentheses after the name "xxx (owner of ... [business name])". Where the plaintiff is a citizen without capacity for litigation, in addition to stating the plaintiff's basic information, also list the name, gender, address of the statutory agent or appointed agent, and their relationship with the principal, and annotate the relationship with the plaintiff in parentheses after the name.

For group litigation cases where litigation representatives are selected or designated, after the plaintiff's identity information, state "Plaintiff and litigation representative ..." and state the basic information of the litigation representative, in the same format as the plaintiff's basic information. If there are many plaintiffs, only the basic information of the litigation representatives may be listed in the heading, and the list of plaintiffs and their basic identity information may be included in the appendix to the judgment.

4. In the administrative judgment, the defendant shall be stated as the name and address of the administrative entity being sued; on a new line, list the legal representative's or litigation representative's name, gender, and position; on another new line, list the basic items of the agent ad litem.

5. Where a third party participates in the proceedings, the third party is listed after the defendant, and the basic information of the third party is written in the same manner.

6. The description of the origin of the case, composition of the trial panel, response of the defendant and third party, exchange of evidence between the parties, and the hearing process is to demonstrate the openness and transparency of the court's judicial activities. If a third party participates in the proceedings, the following format may be used: "Because xxx has a legal interest in the specific administrative act under suit in this case, this Court notified it in accordance with the law to participate as a third party (when a citizen, legal person, or other organization applies to participate as a third party, state: Because xxx has a legal interest in the specific administrative act under suit in this case, upon application by xxx, this Court granted permission for it to participate as a third party)". If a party fails to appear after two lawful summonses without justifiable reasons, it shall be stated: "The [plaintiff/defendant] xxx, after two lawful summonses by this Court, failed to appear without justifiable reasons". If there was an exchange of evidence, it shall be stated: "This Court organized the plaintiff, defendant, and third party to exchange evidence on [date] and served copies of the evidence list". If there was an approved extension of the trial period, the document number of the approval for the extension shall be stated. If a case was heard in a closed session, the reasons for the closure shall be stated. Relevant procedural activities may be described in chronological order.

II. Facts

The facts section shall state the content of the administrative dispute between the parties, as well as the facts and evidence confirmed by the court after trial. The operation method for this part is:

1. Describe in detail the administrative procedures of the specific administrative act carried out by the defendant and the main content of the specific administrative act (including the facts found, legal norms applied, and the result of the disposition), so that the "facts" that need to be reviewed for legality are fully displayed. If the administrative act under suit is not a formal act, the content of the specific administrative act may be determined by reference to the internal report made by the defendant when making the administrative act or the conclusions agreed upon by both parties during the trial.

2. In accordance with the provisions of the Administrative Procedure Law and the "Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Administrative Litigation", the defendant bears the burden of proof for the specific administrative act it has made. To highlight this principle, after the specific administrative act under suit is displayed, the evidence on which the defendant relies to claim the legality of the specific administrative act shall be listed afterwards. The evidence listed shall state the name and content of the evidence, and the purpose of the evidence (may be summarized and categorized according to the defendant's sequence of evidence presentation; or, depending on the case, evidence and basis may be classified and listed from aspects such as statutory authority, enforcement procedure, fact-finding, and application of law; or evidence may be comprehensively listed with non-contentious parts briefly stated). To reflect the requirement that the defendant must provide evidence to the court within the statutory time limit, the time when the defendant provided the evidence shall be stated. If evidence is provided after a court-approved extension, it shall be noted.

3. Briefly summarize the plaintiff's claims and reasons, avoiding copying the complaint or detailing the specific reasoning in the claims. After the plaintiff's claims, state the evidence provided by the plaintiff. If a third party participates in the proceedings, briefly summarize the third party's opinions and the evidence it provided.

4. Summarize the defendant's defenses and requests, taking care to avoid repetition with existing content.

5. Where evidence is obtained by the court ex officio or upon application of the plaintiff or third party, it shall be stated.

6. Points to note in the facts section: (1) The judgment should reflect the dynamic process of the parties' arguments and the court's evaluation of evidence. (2) When preparing the judgment, the case has already been concluded on the merits, and the judge should have a clear understanding, reasonably determine the writing structure, and avoid excessive detail in describing the trial process, focusing on key points. For cases where revocation is to be ordered, the illegal part may be emphasized in the facts and reasons, while other parts may be shortened or omitted. If the review result is that the defendant lacked authority, consideration may be given to stating only the review of statutory authority, supplemented by relevant legal reasoning, without further elaboration on issues such as the enforcement procedure, fact-finding, and application of law of the administrative act under suit. (3) In accordance with Article 54 of the "Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Administrative Litigation", the court's evaluation of evidence should be explained in terms of relevance, legality, and authenticity. For disputed issues, the judge shall follow professional ethics, apply legal provisions, and use logical reasoning and life experience to conduct a comprehensive, objective, and fair analysis and assessment, determining the evidentiary relationship between the evidence materials and the case facts, excluding irrelevant evidence materials, and accurately establishing the case facts. (4) Through in-court examination of evidence or exchange of evidence, if the defendant's admissions to the plaintiff's grounds are consistent with the facts found by the court, it need only be noted; if inconsistent and affecting the establishment of the legality of the specific administrative act, the legality of that part of the facts shall be evaluated after the evidence examination. (5) In accordance with Article 41 of the Administrative Procedure Law and Article 4 of the "Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Administrative Litigation", when a citizen, legal person, or other organization files a lawsuit with the court, it shall provide corresponding evidence materials to prove that it meets the conditions for filing a lawsuit. If a hearing is held on whether the plaintiff meets the conditions for filing a lawsuit, the judgment shall state the trial and evidence examination. If necessary, this may be explained in the judgment: "When filing the lawsuit, the plaintiff provided evidence materials such as ... to prove ... (mainly stating that the plaintiff proved that the specific administrative act under suit objectively exists and that its lawsuit meets the conditions for filing)". (6) If the defendant fails to provide evidence, the format "Defendant xxx did not submit evidence and basis for making the specific administrative act to this Court within the statutory time limit" shall be used; if the defendant submits evidence beyond the time limit, the basis and reason for the court's acceptance or non-acceptance of the evidence shall be stated; if the defendant applies for an extension to provide evidence, state: "The defendant, on the grounds of xxx, submitted a written application for an extension to provide evidence to this Court on [date], and with the permission of this Court, the defendant provided evidence on [date]". (7) If the court obtains evidence ex officio (or upon application of the plaintiff or third party), the name of the evidence obtained, its purpose, and the views of both parties (or the third party) shall be stated; if the court does not permit the obtaining of evidence or fails to obtain the relevant evidence, this shall also be explained. Evidence obtained by the court upon application of the plaintiff or third party shall be treated as evidence of the plaintiff or third party, and in the description of in-court evidence examination, it may be categorized as evidence provided by the plaintiff or third party as the subject of evidence examination. (8) If, upon application of the plaintiff (or third party, defendant), an appraisal department is entrusted to conduct an appraisal, the appraisal department, appraisal matter, appraisal conclusion, and the views of both parties (or the third party) shall be stated. (9) When stating facts, attention shall be paid to preserving state secrets and protecting the reputation of the parties.

III. Reasons

Given the characteristics of administrative litigation, the reasons section shall, based on the facts found and relevant laws, regulations, and legal theories, analyze and demonstrate whether the specific administrative act made by the administrative entity is lawful and whether the plaintiff's claims are well-founded, and clarify the reasoning for the judgment.

The discussion on the legality of the specific administrative act under suit includes: 1. Whether the defendant has statutory authority; 2. Whether the specific administrative act under suit conforms to statutory procedures; 3. Whether the facts found in the specific administrative act under suit are clear and whether the main evidence is sufficient; 4. Whether the application of laws, regulations, judicial interpretations, rules, and other normative documents is correct; 5. Whether the defendant has exceeded its authority or abused its powers, and whether the administrative penalty is manifestly unjust.

Legal analysis shall be carried out with reference to legal norms, and the citation of legal provisions shall be accurate. In accordance with the Administrative Procedure Law and the "Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Implementing the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China", administrative cases shall be tried with reference to laws, administrative regulations, local regulations, autonomous regulations, and special regulations, and with reference to administrative rules formulated and issued by the ministries and commissions of the State Council, as well as by the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, municipalities directly under the Central Government, and larger cities.

In the application of the final judgment basis, the provisions of Article 54(1), (2), (3), and (4) of the Administrative Procedure Law and the relevant provisions of judicial interpretations shall be respectively applied, and when citing, the most specific articles, paragraphs, items, and sub-items shall be stated.

IV. Judgment Result

The judgment constitutes the court's substantive disposition of the administrative litigation dispute between the parties. Pursuant to Article 54 of the Administrative Litigation Law and Articles 56, 57, and 58 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Litigation Law of the PRC, first-instance administrative judgments in as-type cases may be categorized as judgments upholding, judgments revoking or partially revoking, judgments modifying, judgments confirming, and judgments dismissing claims. Where the plaintiff concurrently brings an administrative compensation claim and the court, upon review, finds that the cases may be tried together, the administrative compensation may be addressed as one of the plaintiff's claims in the judgment, and the judgment result shall be either "dismiss the plaintiff's compensation claim" or "order the defendant to pay compensation."

V. Closing

The closing shall state, in order, the allocation of litigation costs, inform the parties of the right to appeal, the method and time limit for appeal, and the appellate court, followed by the signatures of the collegial panel members, the date of judgment, and the signature of the clerk. For cases involving foreign elements, the time limit for appeal shall be governed by the provisions of the Civil Procedure Law.

The official copy of the judgment shall bear the stamp "This copy is verified as identical to the original" at the lower left of the date of judgment and above the signature of the clerk.

VI. Appendix

Depending on the needs of the case, relevant content from the judgment may be included in the appendix, such as attaching the legal provisions cited in the judgment to allow the parties to fully understand the relevant legal provisions. For example, in class action cases, the list of plaintiffs and their identifying information may also be included in this part.

Notes on Form 2

I. This judgment form is for use by courts at all levels when concluding first-instance proceedings under the Administrative Litigation Law in cases of administrative omission (limited to delay and failure to respond) and making a substantive disposition of the case.

II. The heading, closing (including the appendix), and structure of evidence presentation, authentication, reasoning, and related drafting requirements in the judgment may refer to the form and notes for first-instance as-type administrative judgment.

III. The burden of proof in administrative omission cases differs from that in administrative action cases, and this should be reflected in the judgment. The plaintiff shall provide evidence that it has submitted an application to the defendant administrative organ and evidence of the defendant's omission. The defendant shall provide evidence to prove whether the subject matter of the plaintiff's application falls within its statutory duties or obligations, whether it has performed its statutory duties or obligations within the statutory time limit, and whether its omission complies with the law. The judgment shall list relevant evidence according to the conditions set by the substantive administrative law, authenticate the evidence presented by each party, provide sufficient reasoning and argumentation on the basis of authentication, and finally determine whether the defendant's omission is lawful and whether the plaintiff's application is well-founded.

IV. For cases with complex facts and a large amount of evidence, the process of presenting and cross-examining evidence may be categorized and presented at different levels. For cases with simple facts and a small amount of evidence, cross-examination may be conducted collectively after the defendant has presented all evidence.

V. Pursuant to the Supreme People's Court's Several Provisions on Evidence in Administrative Litigation, if the opposing party expressly acknowledges the evidence presented by a party, the probative value of such evidence may be recognized. Authentication of such evidence may be simply stated as: "The [plaintiff/defendant] acknowledges the evidence presented by the [defendant/plaintiff]. This court confirms it."

VI. When finding facts, the court may first directly recognize facts that are not disputed by the parties, as needed: "The plaintiff has no objection to fact X, and the defendant has no objection to fact Y. The above facts are recognized by this court." Then, based on valid evidence, analyze and determine the facts in dispute between the parties.

For cases with simple facts, a small amount of evidence, and minor disputes between the parties over facts and evidence, authentication and fact-finding may be combined in a single statement to avoid unnecessary repetition.

VII. Where the plaintiff concurrently brings an administrative compensation claim when filing an administrative lawsuit against a specific administrative act, and the court, upon review, finds that the cases may be tried together, the administrative compensation may be addressed as one of the plaintiff's claims in the judgment, and the judgment result shall be in the form of "dismiss the plaintiff's compensation claim" or "order the defendant to pay compensation."

Notes on Form 3

I. This judgment form is for use by courts at all levels when concluding first-instance proceedings under the Administrative Litigation Law in cases where a party independently files an administrative compensation lawsuit and making a substantive disposition on the issue of compensation.

A party may file an administrative compensation lawsuit against both specific administrative acts and factual administrative acts of an administrative organ. "Factual administrative acts" refer to unlawful acts of an administrative organ that are not official acts but are related to official acts.

II. The heading, closing (appendix), and structure of evidence presentation, authentication, reasoning, and related drafting requirements in the judgment may refer to the form and notes for first-instance as-type administrative judgment.

III. Where the plaintiff concurrently brings an administrative compensation lawsuit when filing an administrative lawsuit against a specific administrative act, separate judgments may be made, or a single judgment may be made. When making a single judgment, the administrative compensation may be addressed as one of the plaintiff's claims. It should be noted that the term "separate case filing" in Article 28 of the Supreme People's Court's Several Provisions on Issues Concerning the Trial of Administrative Compensation Cases means that for cases involving two claims filed together, separate case files should be established under the principle of one case, one number per year and instance. If the court, upon review, finds that the cases may be tried together, the two separately filed cases shall be returned to the case registration office for cancellation, and the two cases to be tried together shall be re-filed as one case with a new number.

IV. The trial of administrative compensation cases shall be predicated on the unlawfulness of the administrative act at issue. Where the plaintiff files a compensation lawsuit based on a factual administrative act, the judgment shall be based on the defendant's evidence to determine whether the factual administrative act at issue exists. Where the plaintiff concurrently brings an administrative compensation lawsuit when filing an administrative lawsuit against a specific administrative act, the judgment shall be based on whether the specific administrative act at issue has been confirmed as lawful in the administrative judgment.

In compensation proceedings, the facts that a party has suffered losses due to infringement by the administrative act at issue shall be proven according to the rule "he who asserts must prove."

The focus of argumentation in an administrative compensation judgment is whether the factual administrative act at issue exists, whether the specific administrative act at issue is lawful; whether the plaintiff has lawful rights and interests, whether the plaintiff's lawful rights and interests have been infringed upon, the extent and consequences of such infringement, the causal connection with the specific administrative act or factual administrative act at issue, and whether the plaintiff is entitled to compensation. For factual administrative acts that have not been finally determined, determine whether such acts exist based on the defendant's evidence. For specific administrative acts that have been confirmed as unlawful, it is sufficient to state "the illegality of such act has been confirmed by [name of organ]" without further analysis or argumentation.

V. When applying the law in an administrative compensation judgment, it is necessary to apply not only the Administrative Litigation Law but also the State Compensation Law and the provisions of the Supreme People's Court's Several Provisions on Issues Concerning the Trial of Administrative Compensation Cases and other judicial interpretations on administrative compensation.

VI. No litigation fees shall be charged for administrative compensation lawsuits.
